requirements.evidence: The routes match the contract in routes/web.php:20-42: Route::livewire login/register behind guest, POST logout behind auth, home behind ['auth','verified'], password.email with throttle:6,1, and verification.verify with ['auth','signed','throttle:6,1']. Login (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:27-50) validates with email:rfc,strict, keys the limiter on lowercase e-mail + IP with 5 tries, uses auth.failed / auth.throttle on email, regenerates the session and calls redirectIntended(route('home')). Register uses the 'register|'.$ip transliterated key, Password::defaults() and fires Registered through RegisterUser. Reset rotates remember_token (PasswordResetController.php:60-63), fires PasswordReset and has a single email input. VerifyEmailController uses EmailVerificationRequest, so a tampered id gets 403. The resend controller returns home for verified users. .env.example, phpunit.xml and both ui.php files are in place. Gap: requirement 9 says the route() rule also applies to the existing views (welcome, bulma-test). Neither is in the diff, so compliance rests only on the new ViewConventionsTest and cannot be confirmed from the diff.

conventions.evidence: The domain write goes through app/Actions/RegisterUser.php. Login uses #[Validate] + $this->validate(). The reset controller has a Form Request (ResetPasswordRequest) because it has three shared rules. There is a reusable anonymous Blade component (components/form-field.blade.php) with @props and {{ }} escaping. Views and controllers use route() and named redirects. CHANGELOG is updated under [Unreleased]. Deviations: Register uses a protected rules() method (Register.php:53-60) instead of the project's #[Validate] pattern. The layout falls back to a CDN Bulma <link> (layouts/app.blade.php:9-13) instead of only the project's Vite/SCSS pipeline.

security.evidence: Both Livewire actions re-check guest state server-side (ensureGuest, abort_if(Auth::check(), 403)) because update requests skip the page middleware. Every public property is validated. Login and register are rate-limited inside the method. Logout invalidates the session and calls regenerateToken. Forgot-password always returns passwords.sent. The reset rotates remember_token. Verification uses EmailVerificationRequest plus the signed and throttle middleware. $fillable is unchanged and output is escaped. Minor point: the layout loads Bulma from cdn.jsdelivr.net with no integrity/SRI attribute when no Vite build exists (layouts/app.blade.php:12).

tests.evidence: Every requirement has a test. LoginTest covers happy path, session regeneration, case-insensitive e-mail, malformed e-mail, auth.failed, lockout with the auth.throttle text, lockout scoped to one e-mail, the limiter key, and a signed-in user calling submit (unauthorized call). RegisterTest covers the password-rule dataset, confirmed, unique, the IP limiter, and the unauthorized call. PasswordResetTest covers the generic status, the 429 on the 7th request, a single name="email", remember_token rotation, the PasswordReset event and an invalid token. EmailVerificationTest covers the tampered id (403, nobody verified), another user's signed link, throttling, and resend for verified/unverified users. LocalizationTest checks pt_BR vs en. ViewConventionsTest scans every view. Nit: 'remember me rotates the remember token' (LoginTest.php:140-149) only asserts the token is not null.

simplicity.evidence: The code is lean: Route::view for home, the framework's EmailVerificationRequest and Password broker, and one form-field component reused in every form. Small duplication: ensureGuest() is copied verbatim into Login.php:55-58 and Register.php:65-68. The CDN-fallback branch in the layout is extra logic the task did not need.

readability.evidence: Methods are small and well named, with PHPDoc explaining the non-obvious parts (e.g. 'Livewire update requests do not run the page's `guest` middleware'). Translation keys are grouped by screen in ui.php. There is no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the auth/localization task. There are no SCSS/JS, Docker or mail-theme changes. The phpunit.xml edit only adds the two locale pins.

issues.explanation: Requirement 9 explicitly covers the existing views, but the diff leaves them untouched; only ViewConventionsTest asserts compliance, so the diff alone cannot show they use route().
Validation uses a rules() method instead of the project's #[Validate] attribute pattern, unlike the sibling Login component.
The fallback loads Bulma from a third-party CDN with no integrity/crossorigin attributes, bypassing the project's Vite/SCSS pipeline.
ensureGuest() is duplicated in both components.
The 'lowercase' rule rejects mixed-case e-mails on registration instead of normalizing them, while login and reset lowercase the input; this is inconsistent UX.
The test name claims the remember token rotates, but it only asserts the token is not null.

review.summary: The change implements the full session-auth flow (Livewire login/register, logout, home, forgot/reset password, e-mail verification) with pt_BR/en translations, the locale pins and a thorough Pest suite that includes unauthorized-call and tamper tests. Security handling is solid: server-side guest checks, rate limiting, session/token rotation and no e-mail enumeration. Only small issues remain (Register uses rules() instead of #[Validate], a CDN fallback in the layout, and the existing views are not shown in the diff), so I would approve with nits.
